title: Feelings & Reactions
description: Feelings beyond the basics: relieved, embarrassed, moved, dying to know. Plus the words everyone uses with friends, like galau and gemas, and what each one says about how you feel.

items.registerNotes: Deep, lasting happiness, as in a happy life or marriage: Semoga bahagia (Wishing you every happiness). For being pleased about something, senang is the everyday word.
Saya kecewa dengan pelayanannya (I'm disappointed with the service) is a firm but polite complaint.
The everyday word; terkejut is more formal. Bikin kaget aja (You gave me a fright) is the casual reaction.

items.english: confused; not sure what to do
items.registerNotes: For being puzzled and for being torn: Saya bingung mau pilih yang mana (I can't decide which to pick).

items.cultureNote: Malu is a strong social feeling, about losing face in front of others. Hosts say Jangan malu-malu (Don't be shy) to get guests to help themselves.

items.registerNotes: Proud of someone is bangga sama, or more politely bangga dengan: Aku bangga sama kamu (I'm proud of you).
Said with a breath out once something's over: Lega rasanya (What a relief). Of a room or a road, it means roomy.
Casually kesel. Saya agak kesal is a measured way to say you're annoyed; marah is outright angry.
Mostly casual, and said sebel: Sebel deh. Sulkier than kesal, and often half-joking.
Casually grogi (from English groggy), especially for nerves before speaking or meeting someone new: Aku grogi banget.
Jadi iri, deh (Now I'm jealous) is a friendly, joking reply to someone's good news.
items.pitfallNote: English 'jealous' is two words here: iri when you want what someone else has, cemburu in love.

items.registerNotes: For jealousy over a partner: Pacarnya gampang cemburu (Her boyfriend gets jealous easily).
When a speech, a kind gesture or a wedding brings a lump to your throat: Saya terharu sekali.
A lingering, nervous worry, and more formal than khawatir. Casually people say khawatir, or kepikiran (it's playing on my mind).
Sampai puas means to your heart's content: makan sampai puas (eat as much as you like).
Usually said gemes: the urge to squeeze a chubby baby or a kitten. It can also be exasperation, when someone is being slow or silly.
Sabar, ya (Be patient) comforts someone who's waiting or going through a hard time.
items.cultureNote: Patience and calm are highly valued. Losing your temper in public loses you face, whoever was at fault.

items.english: spirit, enthusiasm; (to someone) you've got this
items.registerNotes: Said on its own to cheer someone on before an exam or a long day: Semangat, ya. Lagi semangat means you're full of energy for something.
Slang for a restless, can't-decide mood, often over love: Lagi galau, ya? With friends, not in formal speech.
What everyone says; the written form is mengantuk. Ngantuk berat (really sleepy) is common after a big lunch.
From sepi (quiet, deserted): left on your own and feeling it. Saya kesepian di sini.

items.english: to love, to be fond of
items.registerNotes: Warmer and softer than cinta, and said to partners, children and family alike: Aku sayang kamu.
items.pitfallNote: It's also 'darling' (Sayang, sudah makan?) and 'a pity' (Sayang sekali), so listen for which one is meant.

items.english: to be grateful, to give thanks
items.registerNotes: Often with a sense of thanks to God: Kita harus bersyukur (We should be grateful for what we have). Syukurlah means 'thank goodness'.
Casually nyesel: Nyesel nggak ikut (I wish I'd gone).
items.pitfallNote: Saya menyesal is real regret or a serious apology. For an everyday sorry, say maaf.

items.registerNotes: From tarik (to pull, as on doors): drawn to something. Saya tertarik dengan budaya Jawa (I'm interested in Javanese culture).
Stronger than English 'curious': it nags at you until you find out. Jadi penasaran (Now I really want to know) is a common reply to a teaser.
